applications Version Options RP2350-USB-C with PIO-USB female port C/C++, MicroPython, Arduino support Comprehensive SDK, dev resources, tutorials to help you easily get started Dual-Core, Dual-Architecture The unique dual-core, dual-architecture capability of RP2350A allows users to choose between a pair of industry-standard ARM Cortex-M33 cores, and a pair of open-hardware Hazard3 cores, giving developers a chance to experiment with the RISC-V architecture in a stable, well-supported environment 15 × multi-function GPIO pins Configurable pin function, allows flexible development and integration Board specifications RP2350A microcontroller chip designed by Raspberry Pi in the United Kingdom Adopts unique dual-core and dual-architecture design: dual ARM Cortex-M33 or dual Hazard3 RISC-V processors support, flexible clock running up to 150 MHz Built-in 520KB Static RAM, with onboard 2MB Flash Type-C port for easier use Supports power supply via Type-C port (PD compatible) Castellated module allows soldering directly to carrier boards USB 1.1 with device and host support Low-power sleep and dormant modes Drag-and-drop programming using mass storage over USB Adapting 15 × multi-function GPIO pins from the RP2350A 2 × SPI, 2 × I2C, 2 × UART, 4 × 12-bit ADC, and 14 × controllable PWM channels Accurate clock and timer on-chip Built-in temperature sensor for real-time monitoring of chip temperature 12 × Programmable I/O (PIO) state machines for custom peripheral support What's On Board Outline Dimensions RP2350-USB-C with PIO-USB female port Wiki:
